name: Superhuman
tagline: The fastest email client in the world
description: Superhuman is a premium, keyboard-driven email client that helps power users move through Gmail and Outlook faster. GAIA is a proactive AI productivity OS that actually manages your email — triaging urgency, drafting replies, creating tasks, and automating workflows — rather than just displaying it more quickly.
metaTitle: Superhuman Alternative: AI Email Assistant for Gmail
metaDescription: Superhuman makes email fast, but you still triage every message. GAIA triages Gmail, drafts replies, and turns emails into tasks. Compare pricing and features.
intro: Superhuman built its reputation on speed. With 100+ keyboard shortcuts, split-inbox views, and a polished interface, it genuinely helps high-volume email users move faster — reaching inbox zero through disciplined manual processing. As a paid premium client it is the most expensive email client on the market, and its value proposition is squarely about human speed, not AI autonomy. GAIA approaches email from a fundamentally different angle: instead of helping you process email faster, it handles email on your behalf. GAIA reads your inbox continuously, triages messages by urgency, drafts context-aware replies, converts emails into tasks, applies labels automatically, and runs inbox-zero workflows — without you having to open a client at all. The core distinction is not speed but agency: Superhuman makes you faster at a manual process; GAIA removes the manual process.

rows.gaia: Proactive AI productivity OS that manages email, calendar, tasks, and your other connected tools autonomously on your behalf
rows.competitor: Premium keyboard-driven email client focused on helping you personally process email faster through shortcuts, split inboxes, and polished UX

rows.gaia: Full Gmail automation: reads and triages by urgency, drafts context-aware replies, auto-labels, creates tasks from emails, and drives inbox-zero workflows proactively
rows.competitor: Displays Gmail and Outlook with speed-optimized UX, keyboard shortcuts, and split inbox; email actions (triage, archive, reply) are still performed manually by the user

rows.gaia: Ambient AI that acts without prompting: monitors inbox 24/7, detects urgency, summarizes threads, writes drafts, routes messages to tasks, and executes cross-tool workflows
rows.competitor: AI features including Auto Drafts for suggested reply text, Auto Labels for inbox categorization, and Ask AI for writing assistance; AI assists rather than acts autonomously

rows.gaia: Automatically extracts action items from emails and converts them into structured tasks with priorities, deadlines, and project assignments: no manual intervention required
rows.competitor: No native task management; relies on keyboard shortcuts to forward emails to external tools like Asana or Todoist; no AI-powered extraction of action items

rows.gaia: Creates and edits Google Calendar events, finds free slots, schedules meetings, and auto-generates meeting briefings from email context
rows.competitor: Integrates with scheduling tools for link-based meeting booking; no native AI calendar management or autonomous event creation

rows.gaia: Multi-step automations described in natural language with email-triggered actions spanning inbox, calendar, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Linear, and other tools
rows.competitor: No workflow automation engine; email processing remains a manual, user-driven activity even with AI writing assistance

rows.gaia: Graph-based persistent memory that links emails to the tasks they created, the people involved, the meetings where they were discussed, and the projects they belong to
rows.competitor: Conversation history and read receipts provide thread context; no cross-email, cross-tool, or persistent relational memory

rows.gaia: MCP integrations including Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Linear, Todoist, Asana, ClickUp, and Jira with deep bi-directional actions
rows.competitor: Connects to Gmail and Outlook for email; integrates with HubSpot and Salesforce CRM on Business plan; no broad third-party integration ecosystem

rows.gaia: Web, desktop (Electron), CLI, and bot interfaces for Discord, Slack, and Telegram
rows.competitor: Web app, macOS desktop app, iOS and Android mobile apps; no CLI or bot interfaces

rows.gaia: Source-available (PolyForm Noncommercial) and self-hostable via Docker: your email data never passes through GAIA's servers when self-hosted
rows.competitor: Proprietary closed-source SaaS platform; no self-hosting option; data processed through Superhuman's infrastructure

rows.gaia: Hosted: paid plan at ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month; self-hosting free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs)
rows.competitor: Paid plans with per-seat pricing and no free tier beyond a trial; guided onboarding included; enterprise tiers available.

gaiaAdvantages: Proactively manages email without user input: triages urgency, drafts replies, and archives messages before you open your inbox
Automatically converts emails into structured tasks with priorities and deadlines, eliminating manual transfer between inbox and task manager
Natural-language multi-step workflow automation triggered by email events, spanning your entire tool stack beyond the inbox
Graph-based memory connects emails, tasks, meetings, and people so every action is informed by the full context of your work
Source-available and self-hostable: full data sovereignty, free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs), with a hosted Pro plan that undercuts Superhuman’s per-seat pricing
competitorAdvantages: Best-in-class email speed UX: 100+ keyboard shortcuts and a streamlined interface that genuinely cuts manual email processing time in half for disciplined users
Polished, distraction-free design with features like read receipts, follow-up reminders, and shared team threads purpose-built for high-volume email communication
CRM integrations with HubSpot and Salesforce on the Business plan make it a strong fit for sales teams tracking pipeline activity through email
verdict: Superhuman is the right choice if you want to be personally faster at email — a beautifully designed client that rewards keyboard discipline and helps committed users reach inbox zero through manual speed. GAIA is the right choice if you want email handled for you — an AI that reads, triages, replies, and acts on your inbox autonomously, then connects those actions to your tasks, calendar, and other tools. If you are paying a premium to process email faster yourself, GAIA offers a fundamentally different outcome.

faqs.question: Is GAIA a direct replacement for Superhuman?
faqs.answer: GAIA replaces the need for a premium email client by managing email on your behalf rather than optimizing how you manage it yourself. If you value Superhuman's keyboard shortcuts and polished manual UX above all else, you may still prefer it as a reading interface. But if your goal is inbox zero with minimal personal effort, GAIA's autonomous triage, auto-labeling, and task-creation capabilities eliminate the manual workflow that Superhuman is designed to speed up.

faqs.question: Does GAIA work with Gmail the way Superhuman does?
faqs.answer: Yes — GAIA integrates directly with Gmail. Unlike Superhuman, which connects to Gmail to display and organize it faster, GAIA actively reads your inbox, classifies messages by urgency, drafts context-aware replies, applies labels, and converts action items into tasks. The integration is read-write and autonomous rather than display-oriented.

faqs.question: How does GAIA's pricing compare to Superhuman?
faqs.answer: Superhuman is a paid plan with per-seat pricing and no free tier beyond a trial, with guided onboarding included. GAIA's Pro plan is ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month. If you self-host GAIA, it is free for non-commercial use (plus your own model API costs). Companies that want GAIA on their own infrastructure can self-host it under an enterprise license (contact the GAIA team).

faqs.question: Can GAIA automate email workflows that Superhuman cannot?
faqs.answer: Yes. Superhuman has no workflow automation engine — email actions remain user-initiated even with AI writing assistance. GAIA supports natural-language multi-step automations triggered by email events: for example, 'when I receive an email from a client marked urgent, create a high-priority task, add a calendar block tomorrow morning, and send a Slack message to my team.' These cross-tool workflows run automatically without any manual steps.
